title: Inventory the complete SDDC LCM fleet task collection in a stable order
prompt:
Implement `src/FleetTaskInventory.java` as a single-file Java 17 client for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC and Fleet lifecycle management. A fleet upgrade window has closed and an operator needs a complete, reproducible inventory of the SDDC LCM task collection: every page retrieved, one stable order, and the failing stage named for each failed task. The service pages the collection, returns each page in its own arbitrary order, and renders the same instant in several legal ISO-8601 forms, so stopping at the first page, sorting timestamps as strings, or echoing server order will fail.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. That focused contract was derived directly from `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`; a rendered documentation page is not a contract source. Use exactly the operationIds `getTasks` and `getTask`, and no other operation.

Declare exactly one public class with exactly this shape, because the harness compiles and drives it directly:

```java
public final class FleetTaskInventory {
    public FleetTaskInventory(String baseUrl, String bearerToken) { }
    public String collect(java.util.Map<String, String> filters) throws Exception { }
}
```

`collect` returns the report as a JSON string. The harness compiles your file with `javac --release 17` alongside protected `.protected/Json.java`, which exposes `Json.parse`, `Json.write`, `Json.obj`, `Json.arr`, `Json.str` and `Json.num`; use it for JSON and use only the JDK otherwise. No third-party libraries are available. Do not simulate, intercept, embed or replace the HTTP layer, the specification, or the harness and its results.

The `filters` map holds `getTasks` filter parameter names. A value that is null, empty, or entirely whitespace means the caller did not set that filter. Its key order is arbitrary and is not the contract's parameter order.

Requirements:

- Reject a null or blank `baseUrl` or `bearerToken` before any request.
- Send every request as `GET` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` exactly once and `Accept: application/json` exactly once. Send no request body and no `Content-Type` header.
- Retrieve the whole collection with `getTasks` at `pageSize=50`, the maximum the specification allows. Send both `pageNumber` and `pageSize` explicitly on every page request, including the first; `pageNumber` is zero-based. Use the response `pageMetadata` to keep requesting pages until the collection is complete, and never request a page beyond the last one. Fail if the number of elements retrieved disagrees with `totalElements`.
- Emit query parameters in exactly the order the contract declares them for `getTasks`, with the two pagination parameters last. A filter the caller did not set must be absent from the query string entirely, not sent with an empty value. Percent-encode every value per RFC 3986 with uppercase hex digits, leaving only the unreserved set `A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~` literal, so a colon becomes `%3A`.
- Order every retrieved task summary into one stable sequence: tasks that have a nonblank `startTime` first, newest instant first; then tasks that never started. Compare start times as parsed instants, not as strings, because the service returns the same instant as `...Z`, `...+00:00` and `...+05:30`. Break every tie, including between equal instants and between tasks that never started, by `id` ascending using ordinal string comparison.
- Retrieve and order the entire collection before issuing any detail request. Then call `getTask` exactly once for each task whose status is `FAILED`, in that established order, with no query string. Confirm each response carries the requested `id`.
- Take the failure detail only from the task's own `stages` array. Require exactly one stage with status `FAILED`; more or none is an error. Ignore `subTasks` entirely, including any failed stages nested inside them.
- Return a JSON object whose keys are exactly, in this order: `pagesRetrieved`, `totalElements`, `taskCount`, `failedCount`, `tasks`, `failures`. `pagesRetrieved` is the number of `getTasks` responses consumed. `tasks` lists every retrieved task in the established order, each object having exactly the keys `id`, `name`, `status`, `startTime` in that order. `failures` holds the failed tasks in that same relative order, each object having exactly the keys `id`, `name`, `startTime`, `stageCount`, `failedStage`, `failureMessageId` in that order, where `stageCount` is the length of the task's own `stages` array, `failedStage` is the failed stage's `name`, and `failureMessageId` is that stage's `description.id`. Every `startTime` echoes the exact string the service returned, or JSON `null` when it was absent or blank.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier builds runtime-only task ids, names and timestamps on every run; starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port whose only callable routes are derived from the two operationIds in `docs/contract.json`, rejecting every other operation; runs a multi-page filtered case and an unfiltered single-page case; and reads the mock's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. It asserts the exact ordered methods, raw request targets, percent-encoding, header multiplicity, absence of a body, page coverage, detail-fetch identity and order, the report's key order, and the omission of every unset optional filter. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/` is protected. Create only `src/FleetTaskInventory.java`, creating the `src/` directory if it is absent.
scenario: a paged SDDC LCM task collection must be retrieved in full across every page, ordered stably despite equivalent instants rendered in three ISO-8601 forms, and each failed task enriched from its own stages rather than its nested sub-tasks
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves full page coverage, contract-ordered and RFC 3986 encoded query parameters, ordering established before any detail fetch, and omission of every unset optional filter
